Based on your experience at the AP®
Reading with student responses, what advice would you offer
teachers to help them improve student performance on the exam?
• When a question is presented with named functions, students should use those function names in their responses.
The chances of making an error are much higher when a response uses the function expression instead of the given
function name. Emphasize to students the likelihood of making an error if not using f and g (or some other function
name). For example: Use ∫
3
(g(x) − f (x)) dx
0
, instead of attempting to use ∫
3

))dx.
